rows.title: AMC 20 rear axle — weak two-piece axle shafts (spun hub / sheared key)
rows.howToFix: The accepted bulletproofing fix is a one-piece axle conversion kit (Yukon, Alloy USA, Omix — sold per model year and for Quadra-Trac vs standard housings). Restorers staying stock instead replace any shaft with a damaged keyway, fit fresh hubs, and torque the hub nut to the factory ~250 ft-lb spec with a new cotter pin (never backing the nut off to line up the pin). For heavily-built rigs the whole AMC 20 is sometimes swapped for a Dana 44.

rows.title: Body tub, floor pans, rockers and firewall rust

Restorers replace the body-mount cups and use new polyurethane body-mount bushings, then seam-seal and undercoat the underside and brush cavity wax into the rockers and tub seams. When the tub is too far gone, a full reproduction steel tub (firewall-to-tailgate) from Willys-Overland/Repli-Tub is the reliable path. Keeping the drain plugs clear and the top sealed prevents a repeat.

Correct caster plus tight, beefier linkage eliminates the wobble rather than masking it.

rows.title: Floor Pan and Frame Rust-Through
rows.howToFix: Inspect the entire cab floor, rocker panels, cab corners, rear frame sections, leaf-spring/shackle mounts, and bed supports by removing carpet and undercoating, then probe all suspect areas with a pick or hammer to identify thin metal and hidden perforation. Any rust-through or heavily scaled structural metal should be cut back to solid steel and repaired with welded replacement floor pans, patch panels, or fabricated 16-18 gauge steel sections; treat surrounding areas with rust converter or epoxy primer, seam sealer, cavity wax, and replace leaking door/window seals to stop future water intrusion. If the frame rails, spring mounts, or major unibody sections are severely compromised, professional structural repair or donor-section replacement is required, and some trucks may be uneconomical to save. Typical costs range from about $500-$1,500 for localized patch repairs to $3,000-$8,000+ for extensive floor, cab corner, and structural rust restoration.

Always install the new O-ring/seal supplied with the module; a poor seal will recreate the leak code. After replacement, clear the codes and complete a drive cycle so the EVAP monitor can re-run and confirm the repair.
